source.title: Interpreting CLIP: Insights on the Robustness to ImageNet Distribution Shifts
source.authors: Jonathan Crabb'e; P. Rodríguez; Vaishaal Shankar; L. Zappella; Arno Blaas

record.tranche_reason: The study concept-probes visual representation directions and measures how many concepts they encode, providing indirect evidence about polysemanticity and its relationship to language supervision rather than testing toy-model superposition or capacity competition.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports outlier-feature kurtosis, privileged-direction scores, pruning effects, and robustness metrics. These do not measure the claim versions recorded here. Cited findings from other work were not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study counts Broden concepts (AP ≥ 0.9) per right singular vector of the zero-shot head in CLIP vision encoders. It uses this count as a proxy for polysemanticity, aiming to find indicators of ImageNet-shift robustness. It never tests capacity pressure, sparsity, geometry, SAEs or feature dimensionality. The models are vision encoders, not LLMs, and the polysemanticity proxy has no baseline or control (no random-direction or untrained comparison). So no version's named effect is measured. The reader's V3 link rests on robustness, which is not capacity pressure, so the inference does not follow.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors' main claims concern outlier features (high kurtosis), which appear only in robust models. They also find that unique concept counts are higher in zero-shot CLIP models but do not indicate robustness, and hypothesise this relates to language supervision. They call CLIP features highly polysemantic from a Broden-based proxy. The language-supervision hypothesis rests mainly on unique-concept counts (Figure 3), not on the per-direction polysemanticity table.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Broden concept probing of vision-encoder representation directions and comparisons across CLIP training data; it does not use the original sparse toy-network setup or its sparsity and geometry measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured concept counts depend on the type of language supervision; the paper reports different results across ImageNet-Captions-t, ImageNet-Captions-td, and ImageNet-Captions-tdt.

fits_no_version.finding: Zero-shot CLIP vision encoders average 3.0–16.0 Broden concepts per head singular direction. ViTs are mostly above 10, ResNets 3–10.5. There is no baseline for what count an arbitrary direction would give.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Directions in the final representation of vision (non-LLM) models encode many human concepts each (polysemanticity in vision encoders).

record.problems: The concept probe uses the Broden dataset and an average-precision threshold of 0.9 as a proxy for polysemanticity. The study does not manipulate or measure capacity pressure, sparsity, or feature importance, and does not establish that language supervision causes the observed differences.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweep or geometry.
No test of whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure; robustness is not a capacity variable.
Vision encoders only, no LLMs, no SAEs.
No comparison of 1-D vs multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Within Table 7, per-direction polysemanticity does not cleanly track language supervision: OpenAI RN50 scores 3.0, while ImageNet-Captions-t/td RN50 score 10.5. The AP ≥ 0.9 criterion can also count co-occurring or correlated concepts (e.g., scene categories) as separate, so the proxy may overstate superposition. The paper cites Toy Models of Superposition only as background.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test sparse features exceeding network dimensions, their overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular toy-model geometry.
Does not test whether feature competition for limited capacity causes polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.

Measures concept counts per representation direction and compares models with different language supervision; it does not directly establish a causal mechanism or test whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
Studies vision encoders, not LLMs, and does not use sparse autoencoders.
Does not use or evaluate SAE features.
Assigns concepts to representation directions but does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: ResNet50 OpenAI
rows.operation_detail: Counted Broden concepts with average precision at least 0.9 per right singular vector and averaged across directions.
rows.measure: Average number of concepts encoded per right singular vector (polysemanticity)
rows.note: The paper uses this average as a proxy for polysemanticity; it does not directly test a capacity-based cause.
rows.check: Concepts-per-SVD-direction in a CLIP vision encoder with no baseline. It measures neither capacity pressure (V2/V3) nor LLM features (V4). The 'observed' state against V3 is unfounded.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Non-robust zero-shot ResNet50 ImageNet-Captions-t, ImageNet-Captions-td, and ImageNet-Captions-tdt models
reader_labels.reason: The models encode multiple Broden concepts per direction despite being described as non-robust, consistent with polysemanticity occurring outside robustness-related capacity pressure (r4-r6).
